task.description: Root-cause ISS-0398: Letflow.Engine.create/2 fails a whole PARALLEL_GATEWAY split at instance-creation time ({:error, {:activation_failed, {:no_matching_join_found, split_node_id}}}) whenever any fork-branch node has more than one outgoing edge (e.g. an EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY) before reaching the matching PARALLEL_GATEWAY join. Read lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex's find_matching_join/2 and walk_to_gateway/3 in full, determine whether this is a deliberate scoping limit or a genuine bug, check existing unit coverage, and propose a scoped fix direction for CODE-DESIGNER -- do not implement.
acceptance_criteria: Exact mechanism identified: which function/clause forces every fork-branch node to have exactly one outgoing edge
Determined whether this is a documented deliberate simplifying assumption or an undocumented bug
Existing test coverage for find_matching_join/2 and walk_to_gateway/3 read and its guaranteed invariants stated
Concrete, scoped fix proposal in prose/pseudocode only (no Elixir code)
Risk assessment: could relaxing the one-outgoing-edge rule cause false-positive join matches against unrelated/nested gateways
REQ-051 design doc/decision record checked for whether this was ever explicitly scoped as single-outgoing-edge-branches-only

result.summary:
STEP 0.5 -- REGISTRY LOOKUP: grepped docs/issues/*.yaml for 'walk_to_gateway', 'no_matching_join', 'find_matching_join', 'block-structured' -- ISS-0398.yaml itself is the only hit. No prior resolved issue covers this symptom class. First occurrence, not a recurrence. (Distinct from ISS-0397, which is a separate, already-filed defect: join_counters: %{} hardcoded in Engine.build_instance_state/3, breaking joins across separate calls -- that blocks join COMPLETION; ISS-0398 blocks instance CREATION, before any join counter is even relevant.)

STEP 1 -- ROOT CAUSE:

1. MECHANISM (lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex lines ~801-862): dispatch_parallel_split/4 calls find_matching_join/2 (line 772) for every PARALLEL_GATEWAY split, which for each of the split's outgoing edges calls walk_to_gateway/3 (line 811) starting at edge.target. walk_to_gateway/3's clause structure (lines 837-862): if the current node is itself a :PARALLEL_GATEWAY, return {:ok, gateway_id} immediately (line 845-846) -- this is the only success path. Otherwise (line 848-859) it looks up the current node's outgoing edges via Enum.filter(...&(&1.source == current_node.id)); the ONLY continuation clause is `[single_edge] -> walk_to_gateway(...)` (line 850) -- an exact one-element list match. Any other edge count for `_other` (line 857) -- zero outgoing edges (a dead end / :END reached) OR more than one outgoing edge (any branching node: EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY, a second nested PARALLEL_GATEWAY split, etc.) -- falls to the catch-all `_other -> :error` clause. find_matching_join/2's Enum.reduce_while (lines 810-822) halts the WHOLE reduction with {:error, :no_matching_join} the instant any single branch's walk_to_gateway/3 call returns :error (line 819-820: `:error -> {:halt, {:error, :no_matching_join}}`), which dispatch_parallel_split/4 (line 773-774) turns into {:error, {:no_matching_join_found, node.id}} -- an error tuple from transition/3 that Letflow.Engine.create/2 (the impure activation-time caller) propagates as {:error, {:activation_failed, {:no_matching_join_found, split_node_id}}}, failing the ENTIRE instance-creation call, not just the offending branch. This matches ISS-0398's reported symptom exactly, confirmed by static trace through the exact clause structure (walk_to_gateway/3's `_other -> :error` catch-all is the precise point of failure) -- ISS-0398.yaml's own description (test/letflow/simulation/req208_meridian_test.exs lines 117-134) independently confirms this against a real running instance with a real EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY (kyc-routing, 3 outgoing edges) inside a fork branch.

2. DELIBERATE ASSUMPTION, NOT A HIDDEN BUG -- but a KNOWN, NEVER-CLOSED OPEN QUESTION: lib/letflow/design/req051-parallel-gateway-split-join.md section 3.3 (lines 267-282) describes find_matching_join/2's algorithm exactly as implemented and states outright: 'walk forward from edge.target ... following each node's own single outgoing edge -- a well-formed single branch path between a split and its join has no internal branching, section 12.4's flagged assumption ... Any other outcome (a branch reaches :END before any PARALLEL_GATEWAY, two branches disagree on which gateway they reach first, or a branch's forward walk runs into a node with more than one outgoing edge before reaching a gateway -- an internally-branching branch, unsupported by this simple walk) returns {:error, :no_matching_join}.' Section 12.4 (lines 631-639), titled literally '`find_matching_join/2`'s block-structured-graph assumption', states: 'Assumes every branch path between a split and its join contains no further branching node before reaching the join... Not verified as enforced by any existing CHK-01..CHK-08 structural check... whether Letflow's structural validator *should* reject such graphs upstream (at create/1 time, REQ-030) is left for REQ-028/029's own CODE-DESIGNER to consider adding a check for, not resolved here.' CONCLUSION: this is a SCOPE GAP explicitly flagged at design time as an open question, never resolved by any later requirement (checked REQ-028/029/030's traceability -- no requirement closed this OQ), not an implementation bug relative to the gate-approved design. REQ-051's own acceptance criteria (test/specs/REQ-051.md, AC1-AC6, all exercised by test/letflow/engine/parallel_gateway_test.exs) only ever test the trivial zero-hop case (three_branch_graph/0: each branch is a single direct edge straight to the join, see parallel_gateway_test.exs lines 43-52) -- no test in the existing suite exercises a multi-hop branch at all, let alone one with an internal branching node. So the limitation is doubly confirmed: explicitly named as unresolved in the design doc, and never contradicted by any shipped test asserting a branching-branch case works.

3. EXISTING TEST COVERAGE: test/letflow/engine/parallel_gateway_test.exs (REQ-051's own unit suite) covers AC1 (split produces N tokens+branch_ids), AC2 (wait/fire boundary), AC3 (cancelled-branch exclusion), AC4 (all-branches-cancelled), AC5 (order-independence/exactly-once), AC6 (VariableMerge.merge/3 reuse) -- all built exclusively on three_branch_graph/0, where every branch is ALREADY POSITIONED on the join node with zero intermediate hops. No test exercises walk_to_gateway/3's multi-hop chain-following behavior (the `[single_edge] -> walk_to_gateway(...)` recursive clause) at all -- that code path is currently UNTESTED by the unit suite; its only real exercise is transitively through req208_meridian_test.exs's simulation-level graphs (which is where ISS-0398 was actually found, and where the KYC/AML branch was worked around specifically to avoid it). Any fix MUST preserve: (a) the zero-hop direct-to-join case (AC1-AC6, three_branch_graph/0), (b) the existing cycle guard (`visited` MapSet, line 838-839 -- prevents infinite recursion on a malformed cyclic graph), (c) the existing disagreement/dead-end failure modes (two branches reaching different PARALLEL_GATEWAY nodes, or a branch reaching :END, must still return {:error, :no_matching_join}) -- none of parallel_gateway_test.exs's 6 AC groups may regress.

4. SCOPED FIX PROPOSAL (prose/pseudocode only, not implemented here -- ELIXIR-DEV's job at WF-03 Step 2/3 after CODE-DESIGNER's design pass):
   Conceptually, walk_to_gateway/3 needs to become a REACHABILITY search (explore every path forward from a branch's origin, not just a single linear chain) rather than a linear-chain-only walk, while still terminating at 'the first PARALLEL_GATEWAY node reached on every path out of this branch.' Two candidate approaches:
   (a) BFS/DFS-with-frontier over ALL of a node's outgoing edges instead of requiring exactly one: when a node has >1 outgoing edge (an EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY or a nested PARALLEL_GATEWAY split), recurse into EVERY target instead of erroring, and require ALL such paths from that branch to agree on the same first-reached PARALLEL_GATEWAY node before the branch as a whole is considered resolved (mirrors find_matching_join/2's own existing cross-branch agreement rule, just applied one level deeper, within a branch, before it is applied across branches). A branch's own internal paths disagreeing (e.g. one EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY edge reaches the intended join, but another of its edges reaches :END, or a different gateway) should still be a genuine {:error, :no_matching_join} -- that graph shape really is ambiguous, not a bug in the search.
   (b) Termination condition change: instead of 'every branch node must have exactly one outgoing edge until the join', the walk should stop descending into a subtree as soon as EITHER a PARALLEL_GATEWAY is reached (success leaf) OR a dead end (:END, or a node whose outgoing edges are already exhausted) is reached (failure leaf) -- collect the full set of leaves reached from a branch's origin, and require it to be a SINGLETON set containing exactly one PARALLEL_GATEWAY id (any :END leaf, or more than one distinct PARALLEL_GATEWAY id, is still {:error, :no_matching_join}).
   Both formulations are the same algorithm restated; (b) frames it more directly as 'explore the whole subtree, not just a single strand.' The `visited` cycle guard generalizes unchanged (per-path visited set, not global, to correctly allow two different EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY edges from the SAME upstream node to independently revisit shared downstream nodes without falsely tripping the cycle guard against each other -- CODE-DESIGNER should treat this per-path-vs-global visited-set distinction as a first-class design decision, not an afterthought, since getting it backwards would either miss real cycles or falsely reject legitimate reconverging-then-diverging-again graph shapes).

5. RISK -- false-positive join matching against nested/unrelated PARALLEL_GATEWAY nodes: YES, this is real and must be a named design constraint, not just an implementation detail. Consider a fork branch that itself contains a NESTED PARALLEL_GATEWAY split-then-join pair entirely inside the branch, before reaching the outer join. Under a naive 'first PARALLEL_GATEWAY reached on every path' rule, the search would stop at the INNER join (also a PARALLEL_GATEWAY node) and incorrectly report that inner join as the outer split's matching join -- silently associating the wrong JoinCounter cohort with the wrong split, which would corrupt join_counters bookkeeping (dispatch_parallel_join/4 keys everything by node.id) rather than merely erroring. This is a strictly worse failure mode than today's honest {:error, :no_matching_join_found} -- a WRONG match that appears to succeed, rather than a correct match that fails to be found. CODE-DESIGNER must explicitly decide (and state in the design doc, per this project's OQ-flagging convention) whether nested PARALLEL_GATEWAY split/join pairs fully contained within one branch are in scope for this fix at all: the minimal, lowest-risk fix is to broaden walk_to_gateway/3's traversal ONLY across non-PARALLEL_GATEWAY branching nodes (EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY, or any future branching node type) while leaving 'first PARALLEL_GATEWAY reached, on any path, is treated as this branch's join candidate' unchanged and UNTESTED/OUT OF SCOPE for nested-parallel-within-a-branch (explicitly flagged as a still-open follow-on question, exactly like the design doc's own section 12.4 precedent), rather than attempting to fully solve arbitrary nested fork/join structures in this one fix. ISS-0398's own reported symptom (EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY inside a branch) does not require solving the nested-PARALLEL_GATEWAY case at all -- scoping the fix to 'branching via non-PARALLEL_GATEWAY node types only' fully resolves the reported symptom with materially lower correctness risk, and is the recommended scope boundary for CODE-DESIGNER to adopt (with the nested-parallel case named as an explicit non-goal/OQ in the design doc, not silently ignored).

6. REQ-051 REFERENCE: Confirmed via lib/letflow/design/req051-parallel-gateway-split-join.md sections 3.3 and 12.4 (quoted above) that this limitation was EXPLICITLY SCOPED as a known open question at design time ('block-structured-graph assumption', section 12.4) -- not silently assumed, and not contradicted anywhere in REQ-051's shipped acceptance criteria or test suite. This is a SCOPE GAP that was flagged for 'REQ-028/029's own CODE-DESIGNER to consider' and never actually picked up by any later requirement (no REQ found in docs/requirements.yaml that references req051's section 12.4 OQ or adds a structural CHK-* rule rejecting non-block-structured PARALLEL_GATEWAY graphs). No decision record (docs/migration/decisions/) addresses this either -- it is purely an unresolved design-doc OQ, appropriate for a normal CODE-DESIGNER fix pass rather than a REVIEWER escalation over a contradicted decision record.
issues: REQ-051 design doc section 12.4's open question ('should Letflow's structural validator reject non-block-structured PARALLEL_GATEWAY graphs upstream, at create/1 time, REQ-030') was never picked up by any later requirement -- CODE-DESIGNER should decide, as part of this fix's design, whether the corrected walk_to_gateway/3 is sufficient on its own, or whether an additional upstream structural CHK-* validation (REQ-028/029/030's graph validator) should also be added so a genuinely unsupported graph shape (e.g. a branch that truly has no unique matching join) is rejected at definition-validation time with a clearer error than a runtime {:activation_failed, {:no_matching_join_found, ...}} at instance-creation time. Flagging for CODE-DESIGNER's judgment, not resolving here (out of ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis-only scope).

The nested-PARALLEL_GATEWAY-within-a-branch case (section 5 above) is a real correctness risk if the fix's traversal is broadened carelessly -- recommend CODE-DESIGNER explicitly scope the fix to non-PARALLEL_GATEWAY branching nodes only and name the nested case as an out-of-scope follow-on, mirroring the design doc's own existing OQ-flagging convention (section 12.4) rather than attempting to solve it silently or leave it silently unconsidered.
result.next_action: ORCH routes to CODE-DESIGNER (WF-03 Step 2) for a fix design targeting lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex's walk_to_gateway/3 and find_matching_join/2 -- correctness-sensitive Engine internals warrant a design pass before ELIXIR-DEV implements, per this project's design-gate discipline for join-matching logic.
